headline: High risk of shared-workspace write conflicts and medium prompt/data leakage from marketing outputs into Plandex’s code workspace.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Agent A writes marketing files and builds on shared context; agent B reads/writes a project directory with review-then-apply flow. If A’s content is copied into B’s plan or files, B may treat attacker-controlled text as instructions. No direct shared channel is documented, so this is inferred from both profiles.
conditions: IF A’s output is pasted into B’s plan or project files without sanitization
IF B parses file content as instructions during review-then-apply
mitigations: Use a strict prompt delimiter for any copied text
Review A-generated text before placing it in B’s workspace
Disable auto-apply for cross-agent handoffs
requires-engineering: add provenance tags to imported content

B_data_leakage.rationale: A touches marketing and product-marketing context, while B works in a project directory and can call external APIs with broad egress. If the same workspace contains sensitive marketing material or secrets, B can upload file contents to third parties by default. A’s allowlisted egress is narrower, but B’s broader egress dominates the leakage pathway.
conditions: IF sensitive marketing or secret material is stored in B’s project directory
IF B sends file contents to its model provider or Plandex Cloud
mitigations: Keep sensitive files out of the shared project directory
Redact secrets before B runs
Restrict B to a local/self-hosted backend
Audit outbound requests for file-content uploads
requires-engineering: enforce per-file egress allowlists

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Both agents can read and write files, and B can modify git state while A supports multiple instances and shared context. That creates a direct write-write conflict on the same workspace, with possible irreversible repository corruption or lost changes. The profiles do not show locking or isolation between them.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same repository or directory
IF A and B run concurrently without external locking
mitigations: Run only one agent at a time on the repo
Use separate working copies
Commit or stash before switching agents
Disable B’s git writes during A’s session
requires-engineering: add workspace locks

D_cascading_error.rationale: A produces marketing content and shared context; B’s review-then-apply workflow can treat upstream output as authoritative when generating or applying changes. That creates a plausible cascade from A’s unverified text into B’s actions, but B’s sandbox and staged apply reduce the blast radius below high.
conditions: IF B uses A’s output as source material for plans or edits
IF B applies changes without independent verification
mitigations: Require a human review step between agents
Ask B to restate assumptions before applying changes
Compare B’s plan against source documents
Keep A outputs read-only until validated

E_compliance.rationale: A is a marketing agent with allowlisted egress and B is a coding agent with broad egress and model-provider API use. The profiles do not show regulated data classes like PHI or EU PII, so the main issue is a modest policy mismatch around retention and outbound handling rather than a clear residency breach. Only B is cited because the compliance concern is driven by its broader external transmission.
conditions: IF regulated personal data is placed into either agent’s workspace
IF B transmits that data to a third-party model provider
mitigations: Avoid regulated data in both tools
Use a self-hosted backend for B
Review retention settings before use
Separate marketing and code workspaces
